You can find **olive oil** in a variety of places, depending on your location and preferences. Here are some common options:

### **1. Grocery & Supermarkets**
   - **Major Chains**: Walmart, Kroger, Safeway, Tesco, Carrefour, etc.
   - **Specialty Sections**: Often in the cooking oil aisle, Mediterranean/International section, or organic/health food area.
   - **Brands to Look For**: Bertolli, Colavita, Filippo Berio, California Olive Ranch, Cobram Estate, etc.

### **2. Specialty & Gourmet Stores**
   - **Olive Oil Shops**: Some stores specialize in high-quality olive oils (e.g., **Olive & Coco** in the U.S., **Oliviers & Co** in Europe).
   - **Italian/Mediterranean Markets**: Often carry imported, premium olive oils (e.g., **Eataly**, local delis).
   - **Farmers' Markets**: Local producers may sell fresh, cold-pressed olive oil.

### **3. Online Retailers**
   - **Amazon** ([www.amazon.com](https://www.amazon.com)) – Wide variety, from budget to premium.
   - **Thrive Market** ([thrivemarket.com](https://thrivemarket.com)) – Organic & specialty oils.
   - **Olive Oil Direct importers**:
     - **Brightland** ([brightland.co](https://brightland.co)) – Premium California olive oils.
     - **Cobram Estate** ([cobramestate.com](https://www.cobramestate.com))
     - **Kosterina** ([kosterina.com](https://kosterina.com)) – Greek olive oil.
     - **Zoe Olive Oil** ([zoeoliveoil.com](https://www.zoeoliveoil.com)) – Single-origin oils.
   - **iHerb** ([www.iherb.com](https://www.iherb.com)) – Good for organic options.

### **4. Warehouse Clubs (Bulk Buying)**
   - **Costco, Sam’s Club, BJ’s** – Often sell large bottles of extra virgin olive oil at good prices.

### **5. Direct from Producers (Best for Freshness)**
   - Many olive oil farms sell directly through their websites. Some well-known regions:
     - **Italy**: Tuscany, Puglia, Sicily (e.g., **Badia a Coltibuono**, **Tenuta di Capezzana**)
     - **Spain**: Andalusia (e.g., **Picual**, **Hojiblanca** varieties)
     - **Greece**: Crete, Peloponnese (e.g., **Terra Creta**, **Gaea**)
     - **USA**: California (e.g., **Lucero**, **McEvoy Ranch**)
     - **Australia**: Cobram Estate, Boundary Bend

### **6. Discount Stores**
   - **Trader Joe’s** – Affordable, good-quality EVOO.
   - **Aldi, Lidl** – Often have decent imported olive oil at low prices.

### **What to Look For When Buying:**
✅ **Extra Virgin Olive Oil (EVOO)** – Highest quality, unrefined, best for health.
✅ **Cold-Pressed** – Ensures minimal processing.
✅ **Harvest Date** – Freshness matters (look for recent harvest, ideally within 1-2 years).
✅ **Dark Glass Bottle or Tin** – Protects from light oxidation.
✅ **Origin** – Single-origin oils (e.g., "100% Italian," "California") are often higher quality than blends.
❌ **Avoid**: "Pure," "Light," or "Refined" olive oil (lower quality, processed).

### **Best for Cooking vs. Finishing:**
- **High-heat cooking**: Use a **refined olive oil** or **light olive oil** (higher smoke point).
- **Salads, dipping, finishing**: **Extra virgin olive oil** (best flavor and nutrients).

Would you like recommendations based on a specific budget or use case (e.g., cooking,health, or gourmet)?
